system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft vs. Buyer Playbook

**Scope note:** This review is based on the Seller's summary update and Disclosure Letter. I have not seen the full SPA mark-up, so clause references should be checked against it. Nothing here is Amelia Frost's written authority. Where the playbook allows a fallback only with her approval, I treat that approval as not given.

| ID | Issue | Seller position | Buyer should want (playbook) | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001** | General liability cap | 20% of price, AUD 4.8m (cl. 12.1) | 25% / AUD 6.0m starting position. 20% only as a conditional fallback with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft. | **Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m.** The 20% fallback has not been authorised in writing. |
| **SPA-N-002** | De minimis and basket | De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000 with recovery of the excess only (cl. 12.2) | De minimis AUD 5,000; AUD 50,000 aggregate basket, with the Seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded. | **Reject; counter at AUD 5k de minimis and AUD 50k first-dollar basket.** The Seller's structure excludes most small claims and turns the basket into a deductible. |
| **SPA-N-003** | General claims time limit | 18 months, plus a proposal that any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise (cl. 12.3 / 13) | 24 months after Completion. 18 months is a fallback needing Frost's written approval. No cross-application of general limits. | **Reject; counter at 24 months and delete the "applies to all Claims" language.** The 18-month period is unapproved, and the cross-application wording is a hidden override of the separate regimes. |
| **SPA-N-004** | Fundamental / Title regime | Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties (cl. "administrative simplicity") | Separate regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. | **Reject; restore a separate Fundamental/Title regime.** Folding title into the general regime removes the protection the playbook requires. |
| **SPA-N-005** | Fraud carve-out | Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl. 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5). No fraud carve-out is shown. | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. Non-waivable. | **Reject; insert an express, non-waivable carve-out.** "Any nature" language with no carve-out would cover fraud. |
| **SPA-N-006** | Disclosure scope | General disclosure of the whole data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public records (Disclosure 1.1, 1.2; Sch. 7) | Specific fair disclosure only. Reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure. | **Reject; accept specific disclosure only.** Deemed disclosure of the full data room would disclose away warranty claims without specific notice. |
| **SPA-N-007** | Buyer knowledge qualifier | Buyer has no claim for matters known to it or its advisers, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records (cl. 8.3) | Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry. Never applies to title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity. | **Reject; delete cl. 8.3.** Constructive knowledge of the data room would gut the warranties. |
| **SPA-N-008** | Bluefen consent | Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent (cl. 3 / 6.3). Disclosure 2 confirms no final consent or evidence of conditions. | Effective consent and evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion. Not consent-on-delivery. Reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a material customer consent. | **Reject; make effective consent plus condition evidence a pre-Completion condition.** Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m), and no final consent exists yet. |
| **SPA-N-009** | Riverlark facility | ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release to be provided after Completion (cl. 2 / 7). Disclosure 3 confirms not repaid and no discharge. | Current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases. Post-Completion release only with an irrevocable undertaking and Frost's approval. | **Reject post-Completion release; require a payout letter, direct repayment from funds, and security releases.** About AUD 3.2m of debt would otherwise remain outstanding after Completion. |
| **SPA-N-010** | Employee bonuses (DD-005) | AUD 420k bonuses "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. Payroll tax and on-costs not addressed (Disclosure 5). | AUD 420k plus triggered on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item, or seller-funded. Funds flow must not silently exclude them. | **Reject silent exclusion; itemise AUD 420k and on-costs, or require Seller funding.** The bonuses are absent from the funds flow and the on-costs are unquantified. |
| **SPA-N-011** | Ironquay IP indemnity | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; described as adequate (cl. 11.1). DD-010 records AUD 180k open, not independently verified. | Broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure. The AUD 180k is not independently verified either way. | **Reject as drafted; broaden the indemnity and verify the AUD 180k.** The current indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment and leaves other exposure with the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-012** | Export/privacy incident (DD-006) | Preliminary operational matter, "not expected to be material"; no loss amount (Disclosure 6, Sch. 6) | Preserve logs, investigate and require updates. Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction. | **Hold; require log preservation, investigation updates and scope confirmation.** The Seller's "not expected to be material" is a characterisation the playbook does not adopt. |
| **SPA-N-013** | Sandbar renewals | Three renewals totalling AUD 330k; described as ordinary-course operating costs (cl. 4 / DD-008, DD-011) | Assess. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction. | **Assess; do not accept automatic Debt treatment or a price deduction.** Disclosure 8 does not say whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable or accrued. |
| **SPA-N-014** | Category separation | Tax and IP settled "under the general regime"; the general regime applies to all claim types | Keep Title/Fundamental, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories separate. No hidden general-regime override. | **Reject; keep each category separate.** The Seller's collapsing of categories into one general regime is the override the playbook prohibits. |
| **SPA-N-015** | Title verification | Title evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012 (cl. "Title"; Disclosure 10) | Independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence. DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof. | **Reject DD-012 as sufficient; require independent verification.** An internal share register cannot prove title independently. Independent searches (e.g. ASIC register and encumbrance searches) should be used. |
| **SPA-N-016** | Tax / IP open terms | Tax and IP warranties "settled" under the general regime | Remain open. Assume no unlimited liability and no resolution. | **Hold open; reject the "settled" characterisation.** The playbook keeps Tax/IP open and the Seller's assertion of settlement is not agreed. |

---

### Priority points for the mark-up

1. **Pre-Completion conditions:** Bluefen consent (SPA-N-008) and the Riverlark payout and discharge (SPA-N-009) are the largest exposures, at roughly AUD 3.6m revenue and AUD 3.2m debt.
2. **Funds flow:** The AUD 420k bonuses plus on-costs (SPA-N-010) and the Riverlark repayment must be reflected in the Completion funds flow.
3. **Authority gate:** Do not offer the 20% cap or the 18-month period without Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft.
4. **Fraud and knowledge:** The fraud carve-out (SPA-N-005) and deletion of cl. 8.3 (SPA-N-007) should be resolved before the general regime is discussed, because the Seller's current drafting covers fraud and constructive knowledge.
=== END ADVICE ===
